dedupe_keys.name: nlr sup3rcc generative ai downscaled future climate data 4 km hourly temperature humidity wind and solar for energy system resilience

description: Sup3rCC is an application of Sup3r, the National Laboratory of the Rockies (formerly NREL) open source super-resolution software, that downscales global climate model outputs to 4 km spatial and hourly temporal resolution. Contents: high-resolution future temperature, humidity, wind speed and solar irradiance data generated by a generative machine learning model that learns realistic small-scale spatial and temporal patterns from historical high-resolution data sets, including the National Solar Radiation Database and the WIND Toolkit, and injects them into coarse climate model data. Sister products apply the same software to history: Sup3rWind downscales reanalysis to 2 km and 5 minutes, and Sup3rUHI covers urban heat. Producer: NLR Energy Systems Analysis. Coverage: future climate scenarios; the page does not state the domain on the text read, while the related Sup3rLoad record describes Sup3rCC runs for the contiguous United States. Format and access: open source Sup3r software with documentation (natlabrockies.github.io/sup3r) and publicly available data sets. Licence (read on 2026-09-29): code BSD-3-Clause (sup3r repository); data licence not stated on the pages read. Caveats: the page stresses that Sup3rCC does not represent real historical weather events, so it suits climate statistics, not event reconstruction. Simulation uses: future weather for load, renewable output and thermal derating studies, and climate stress testing of power systems. Related records: data-sup3rload, data-nsrdb-national-solar-radiation-database and data-nlr-cambium-hourly-us-electricity-sector-projections-to-2050.
